title: Unit transitions in strict quotient towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi$, and scheme morphisms $Z\xrightarrow hX\xrightarrow fY$ with $\ell$ invertible on all three schemes [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On compatible small pro-etale sites use the specified inverse images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Put $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$, $R_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$, and let $q^W_{m,n}$ and $\pi^W_n$ be the actual quotient and limit maps for $m\ge n\ge1$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_r$ be a finite, possibly empty, list of integer-indexed K-flat $R_Y$-complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Form finite syntactic expressions from $P_i\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,n}$ at $Y$ and $B_{W,n}[0]$ at $W=Y,X,Z$, by direct-sum total tensor on a common scheme and termwise module pullback along $f,h,f\circ h$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-strict-quotient-expressions]. Distinct syntactic expressions are not identified.

The canonical constant-ring maps $c^g_n:g^{-1}B_{W,n}\xrightarrow\sim B_{W',n}$ satisfy $c^g_n\,g^{-1}q^W_{m,n}=q^{W'}_{m,n}\,c^g_m$ for every permitted $g:W'\to W$. Fixed-level pullback is exact inverse image with its action transported by $c^g_n$.

Every expression has its prescribed complex $K_n$, with flat terms and K-flat over $B_{W,n}$. Its localization computes the corresponding finite expression of derived reduction, derived tensor and derived pullback [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. These comparisons use the prescribed complexes at every intermediate constructor, without replacing them by new resolutions.

The following formulas define compatible semilinear chain maps $t^K_{m,n}:K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]: on a generator $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes q_{m,n}(b)$; on a unit, $b\mapsto q_{m,n}(b)$; on a total-tensor summand, $u\otimes v\mapsto t^U_{m,n}(u)\otimes t^V_{m,n}(v)$; on a pullback scalar generator, $s\otimes u\mapsto q^{W'}_{m,n}(s)\otimes g^{-1}t^U_{m,n}(u)$, using $c^g_m,c^g_n$ for the balancing rings. They commute with all site restrictions and with the total differential $d(u\otimes v)=du\otimes v+(-1)^{\deg u}u\otimes dv$. They satisfy $t^K_{n,n}=1$ and the strict quotient cocycle $t^K_{k,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{k,m}(t^K_{m,n})\,t^K_{k,m}$ for $k\ge m\ge n$, under identity-on-sections scalar restriction composition.

Thus these particular complexes and maps form a complex $K_\bullet$ of strict semilinear systems on the vertical sequence site [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. This complex has flat terms and is K-flat in the module category of that sequence site, with its ordinary total tensor; this assertion concerns system flatness, not flatness after restriction to $R_W$. Its derived evaluations and the evaluations of its system tensor and geometric pullback are computed by the displayed level complexes and constructor comparisons. Restricting each level along $\pi^W_n$ makes every transition $R_W$-linear, giving a complex in $\operatorname{Tow}_{R_W}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(R_W))$. Its localization has evaluations $\operatorname{Res}_n QK_n$ and precisely the localized actual transitions, hence supplies the coherent derived-tower datum (without yet asserting normalization) of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. No boundedness, constructibility, inverse-limit preservation by inverse image, or flatness of a quotient map is assumed.

proof.text: The identity components define a natural transformation from the commutative coefficient sequence, after forgetting commutativity, to the recorded ring sequence. Its naturality identifies every quotient map; evaluating a horizontal product-site arrow therefore gives precisely coefficientFiniteQuotient.

Apply naturality of the underlying abelian-presheaf map of the inverse of singleObjXSelf in degree zero to the horizontal arrow (n,U) to (m,U). Evaluate at b and substitute the preceding identification. This proves the claimed unit equation for arbitrary schemes and levels, independently of the unused generator list. Using the underlying abelian natural transformation avoids unfolding scalar-restriction coherence in the kernel.
